name: Pregabalin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Pregabalin is cleared mainly by the kidneys, and its clearance is nearly proportional to creatinine clearance (CrCl). The US label scales the total daily dose to CrCl and adds a supplemental dose after each 4-hour hemodialysis session.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min; Cockcroft–Gault).

bands.recommendation: Total daily dose 150, 300, 450 or 600 mg/day in 2 or 3 divided doses, by indication (label).
Label band CrCl 30–60: 75, 150, 225 or 300 mg/day in 2 or 3 divided doses (half the normal-function dose).

Label band CrCl 15–30: 25–50, 75, 100–150 or 150 mg/day, once daily or in 2 divided doses. Start at the bottom of the range (25–75 mg/day in CrCl <30 / HD) and titrate slowly; altered mental status and falls are increased in HD patients (Ishida 2018; Muanda 2022).

25, 25–50, 50–75 or 75 mg/day as a single daily dose (label). Start at the bottom of the range (25–75 mg/day in CrCl <30 / HD) and titrate slowly; altered mental status and falls are increased in HD patients (Ishida 2018; Muanda 2022).

hd.text: Dose by CrCl as above, plus one supplemental dose right after every 4-hour hemodialysis: 25 mg/day regimen, 25 or 50 mg; 25–50 mg/day, 50 or 75 mg; 50–75 mg/day, 75 or 100 mg; 75 mg/day, 100 or 150 mg (label). Start at the bottom of the range (25–75 mg/day in CrCl <30 / HD) and titrate slowly; altered mental status and falls are increased in HD patients (Ishida 2018; Muanda 2022).

pd.text: No data in label. Insufficient data: use the CrCl <15 regimen with specialist input.

crrt.text: No data in label. Insufficient data: specialist input.

dialyzable: Yes: about 50% removed in a 4-hour hemodialysis session (label).
monitoring: Dizziness, somnolence, edema, respiratory depression (especially with opioids or other central nervous system depressants). Altered mental status and falls are more common in hemodialysis patients (Ishida 2018).

pediatric.approved_ages: Adjunctive therapy for partial-onset seizures: 1 month and older. Neuropathic pain and fibromyalgia: not established in children (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: Partial-onset seizures: weight 30 kg or more, start 2.5 mg/kg/day, maximum 10 mg/kg/day (not to exceed 600 mg/day), 2 or 3 divided doses. Under 30 kg, start 3.5 mg/kg/day, maximum 14 mg/kg/day; 3 divided doses under 4 years, 2 or 3 doses from 4 years (label).
pediatric.max_dose: 10 mg/kg/day (≥30 kg; not to exceed 600 mg/day) or 14 mg/kg/day (<30 kg) (label).

renal.recommendation: Normal kidney function: usual pediatric dosing (label).
Not studied in children with reduced kidney function (label). Specialist input.
Not studied in children with reduced kidney function (label). Specialist input.
Not studied in children with reduced kidney function (label). Specialist input.

pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)

adult: Label band edges (30–60, 15–30) overlap at 30 and 60; kept as in the label.
pediatric: The label states pediatric use in compromised renal function has not been studied; no pediatric kidney dosing offered. 'ge60' band reads 'not studied' only because the label gives no eGFR qualifier for children; normal-function dosing applies.
